The story you were told about dementia is out of date.

You’ve probably heard what we were taught in medical school: dementia is genetic, it’s bad luck, and nothing can be done until memory starts slipping. The science now tells a very different story. 90% of the risk factors for cognitive decline are modifiable through physician-directed lifestyle protocols.

The brain changes behind Alzheimer’s can begin as many as 20 years before the first forgotten name. That means your 40s, 50s, and 60s aren’t a waiting room. They’re your window.

Healthspan, not just lifespan

This isn’t only about avoiding dementia. It’s about your next 30 years.

Cognitive longevity means being the one who remembers the grandkids’ recital, plans the trip, runs the business, finishes the crossword, and is still the person everyone calls for advice. The root causes we address for your brain also drive energy, sleep, weight, mood, blood pressure, and how fast you age.

Now imagine someone handed you a pill that made that future far more likely. You’d take it without a second thought.

There is no pill. But there is something just as powerful: the small choices you make every day. How and when you eat, how you move and sleep, the light you see, the toxins around you, how you handle stress, and the gratitude, nature, and connection in your life all reach down to your cells: your mitochondria, your cellular energy, your mind-body connection. Each choice either fuels your brain or quietly drains it.

PEAK puts a plan built for your body in your hands, along with the knowledge to choose with confidence. One choice at a time, the future you just pictured becomes something you build every day.

Questions, answered honestly.

Do I need to have memory problems to start?

No — the best time is before anything shows. Most PEAK patients come because they want to keep it that way, often after watching a parent decline.

What if my results are frightening?

Every result arrives with a plan and a physician beside you. We look for risks so we can lower them, not to deliver a verdict.

I carry APOE4 or have a parent with dementia. Is it too late?

Genes load the dice; biology and lifestyle shape how they roll. Dr. Lori carries very high genetic risk herself — and has lowered her biological age by more than 10 years.

How is this different from my regular doctor?

Your physician spends real time with you every month, tests for what standard visits don’t, and addresses root causes rather than waiting for symptoms.

How much time does it take?

About an hour a week for your module and action steps, plus one virtual visit with your physician each month.

Can I do this from outside Texas?

All program visits are virtual, and we serve patients both locally and nationwide. Call us to confirm availability in your state.

Is it covered by insurance?

PEAK is cash-pay. Some patients use HSA or FSA funds, and we can provide documentation. 0% financing for up to 12 months is available through Cherry.

Can my spouse join me?

Yes. Your spouse’s consultation is free when booked with yours, and if you both enroll, you each receive $500 off.

About Us

The physicians of Timarron Family Medicine, and the founders of PEAK Cognitive Longevity.

Why we built PEAK

We know dementia as physicians, and as a daughter and son who watched a parent live with it. We did what we knew to do for our own families, but conventional medicine offered few ways to look for the underlying risks early or a clear path to change them.

That experience changed the questions we asked in our practice. We retrained in root-cause and longevity medicine, and built PEAK to bring families earlier testing, a physician who knows them, and practical steps to support brain health.

If the video doesn’t play, open it in a video player.

PEAK Cognitive Longevity is a physician-led, science-driven program that treats brain health as something to be measured, understood, and actively preserved. Using precision medicine, we evaluate each person's individual risk for cognitive decline, build a protocol designed for them alone, and walk beside them every step — protecting memory, sharpening the mind, and reclaiming the future with confidence.

We believe cognitive decline is far more preventable than most people are told, and that the mind is a gift worth fighting for. This is the climb, and we walk every mile of it beside those we serve.

The Program

What PEAK Actually Includes

Six months. Two things happening at once: a personal clinical relationship, and a structured education that changes how you live.

Weeks 1–2

Testing

Advanced testing done largely from home. We measure your brain with four blood biomarkers, then look at the systems feeding into it: metabolic and cardiovascular health, gut health, vitamins and nutrients, hormones and neurotransmitters, cellular energy, and — depending on your tier — genetics, environmental exposure, and professional cognitive testing.

Weeks 3–4

Analysis & Protocol

Your physician reviews everything, then sits down with you for a full Review of Findings. Together you build a protocol targeting the specific root causes the testing found in you.

Months 2–7

The Climb

One educational module each week — 26 in total, across six monthly Basecamps covering inflammation, mitochondrial health, cellular energy, autophagy, and lifelong brain health. Expect about an hour a week to read and think it through — the action steps happen inside the life you already have.

Every Month

Physician Visit

A one-on-one virtual visit with Dr. Lori or Dr. Chris to adjust your protocol, review supplements, and answer questions. Between visits, you can message your physician directly, any time.

Four Brain Biomarkers, From a Blood Draw

Most brain-health programs never look directly at the brain. We do — with four blood biomarkers that together give a picture of what is happening in your nervous system right now. They are one part of a larger work-up: metabolic health, gut, hormones, nutrients, cellular energy, and, depending on your tier, genetics and toxic exposures are measured alongside them because those systems influence what the brain markers eventually show.

p-Tau 217 — the most reliable blood marker we have for Alzheimer's-type changes in the brain
Amyloid beta 42/40 ratio — whether amyloid is accumulating, and to what degree
NfL (neurofilament light) — a signal of nerve cell injury anywhere in the nervous system
GFAP — a measure of inflammation in the brain's support cells

No single one of these tells the whole story. Read together, they tell us whether anything is happening beneath the surface — years before it would show up in how you think or feel.

Most people go their entire lives without ever knowing where they actually stand. You don't have to be one of them.

At six months, you finish with a PEAK Graduation Session — a full look at what changed and what comes next. Most graduates continue with us into PEAK Ascent, our Year 2 program. That's a decision for later, not now.

A detailed breakdown of each monthly Basecamp and a full comparison of testing tiers is part of what we walk you through at your consultation.

The Evidence

The Research Behind PEAK

The 2024 Lancet Commission identified 14 modifiable risk factors and concluded that nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to factors that can change. PEAK translates that evidence into measurable clinical work across blood pressure, blood sugar, hearing, sleep, inflammation, activity, nutrition, and other contributors to brain health.

Our approach reflects the growing evidence that cognitive decline is influenced by whole-body health over many years. Testing does not predict a personâ€™s future with certainty; it gives physicians an earlier opportunity to identify risks and build a targeted plan.

Established versus emerging

The 14 Lancet risk factors are well established. Other areas we work in — toxicant exposure, hormonal health, and the gut-brain axis — are actively studied and biologically plausible, but the evidence is not yet strong enough to say that treating them prevents dementia. We address them because they influence the systems that shape brain health, while staying clear about what the evidence can and cannot promise.
